newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods move higher NYMEX, heavy buys.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods move higher NYMEX, heavy buys.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot products kept rising amid thin Friday activity, gaining strength from pricier futures and rumors of major refinery buying, brokers said.
"There's major buying interest," one broker said.
NYMEX prices advanced after the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported on Thursday drawdowns in crude oil and distillate supplies.
January gasoline edged up 0.23 cents to 69.74 cents while front-month heating oil climbed 0.49 cents a gallon to 70.55 cents.
Buying pressure also came from traders trying to schedule barrels for second-cycle shipments next week, brokers said.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline were talked one cent higher at 76.50 cents late Friday, while offers rose 1.50 cents to 77.50 a gallon, brokers said.
Conventional gasoline was assessed 74/75 cents a gallon late, up one cent from Thursday.
"It's right in L.A.," a trader said.
Refineries rumored to have production problems were not immediately available or declined comment.
